memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: All the sacred contributions the Israelites bring to a priest will belong to him. Sacred things belong to the owner, but what they give to the priest will belong to the priest. - Num 5:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses deal with the sacred contributions given to the priests. When the people brought their offerings to God, a portion belonged to the priests who served Him. In this way, those who devoted their lives to God's service were provided for through the generosity of the people.

Behind this practical arrangement lies a gracious principle: God provides for those who serve Him, through the giving of His people. The priests owned no farmland like the other tribes; the Lord Himself was their portion. And He met their needs through the offerings brought by others.

This teaches us something about generosity within the family of God. When we give to support God's work and God's servants, we are part of His way of providing for them. Our giving is not merely charity; it is a sacred participation in God's care for His people.

The New Testament carries this forward. Paul writes that "those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel" (1 Cor 9:14), and that generous giving to God's work is like "a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God" (Phil 4:18).

What we give to God, given cheerfully, becomes something holy. It provides for others, it honours God, and it loosens the grip of money on our own hearts.

Give today with an open, joyful hand, knowing that God uses your generosity to care for His people.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you view your giving as a sacred participation in God's work?
- How can you support those who serve God?
- Does money have too tight a grip on your heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You provide for Your servants through the giving of Your people. Make me a cheerful, generous giver for Your work. Amen.
